thread.title: The Bright And The Dark Side Of Apple Valuation - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Oleh Kombaiev
title: The Bright And The Dark Side Of Apple Valuation - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Part 1: The bright side In my opinion, in the next 2 quarters, Apple's ( AAPL ) share price will reach the level of $200 and stay at this level. This will happen not only because of the aggressive buy-back, or the fact that Warren Buffett publicly declared his love for the company and bought 75 million additional Apple’s shares, but also because Apple is now relatively cheap judging by its multiples.
In this context, first of all, it should be noted that judging by the EV/EBITDA, Apple is currently the most underestimated company on the FAAAMG list:
We get the same result analyzing Apple through the EV/FCF:
In the last quarter, Apple's results inspired the market, forcing analysts to raise their expectations regarding the company's earnings in the current and the next year. And now comparing Apple with other companies on the FAAAMG list through the P/E multiple adjusted for the expected earnings growth, we see more than 40% growth potential of Apple’s shares:
If you compare Apple to a broader list of companies using this method, the result is almost the same:
I did a similar comparison in February this year, and then the potential for growth was absent .
By the way, please do not pay attention to the fact that Apple is significantly overrated on the P/S. At the current phase of Apple’s business cycle, when the revenue growth of the company has reached the plateau phase, this multiplier cannot serve as a qualitative indicator of the company’s value .
In the purely technical context, Apple is also in a fairly convenient location for eventual growth, because the current share price is very close to the level of its long-term trend. In other words, Apple's stock is not overpriced now relative to its trend.
Part 2: The dark side I read many positive articles about Apple and periodically make attempts to rethink my vision of this company’s future. But I always face the basic problems of Apple to which I cannot find any solution.
I'll start with the most obvious.
More than 60% of Apple's revenue comes from the iPhone. And this proportion tends to increase. In other words, Apple critically depends on the Smartphone market.
The most rapid growth of Apple’s capitalization fell on the period from 2009 to 2016. This period coincided with the most rapid growth of the global smartphone market that has now reached the "plateau" phase, promising the future growth of no more than 2% YOY. I.e. the quantitative growth of the future iPhone sales has probably also reached the "plateau" phase.
It can be argued that Apple has the opportunity to discover the Indian market and to replicate the success in China's market in the year 2015:
Given the economic potential of India and its demographic structure in which more than 50% of the population is under the age of 25 (and this is the most active buyers of smartphones), the prospects for Apple look really great. However, to date, the average income of the population of India does not allow one to compare the potential of this market with the market of China. And I don’t think anything will significantly change in the next two-three years.
Going further.
I'm not a big fan of Apple products. I am repulsed by the closed nature of its ecosystem. But it is always interesting to follow the releases of new iPhone models. And it's easy to notice that iPhone develops only evolutionarily , there are no revolutionary changes. The screen becomes wider, the frames become thinner, the camera quality gets better, with some additional features such as face detection and wireless charging are being introduced, the battery runs longer etc. But Apple competitors also introduce similar features to their smartphones. Moreover, every new iPhone model is less and less different from the previous one, but more and more expensive. It means that the owners of the previous model have fewer and fewer reasons to buy the new model because it has almost the same features at a higher price.
Apple has always been associated with something fantastic , however, it seems to gradually fade away. Although I understand that such judgments are always subjective and I only express my opinion.
Apple has a huge cash balance, therefore, its dividends will grow and new buy-back programs may appear. That's enough to keep the company's capitalization from falling, but it cannot provide an explosive growth. In order to explode, the company needs a fantastic product and a fantastic market. It has neither the former nor the latter, and this is the main problem.
For more than half a year, Apple's stock price fluctuated around $170. Only the record $23 billion buyback in the first quarter and Warren Buffett, who bought the stock for additional ~$13 billion, helped to break through the resistance at the level of $180. But can we count on a similar coincidence of circumstances in the future?
Putting It All Together So, as I’ve already said, Apple’s stock price has all chances to rise to $200, because the multiples point to this, and people love round numbers. However, I don’t see the reason to forecast the further growth of Apple’s capitalization in the near future.
